paragraphs.title: Gog’s Commission and the Preparation of His Army

easy.explanation: The Lord tells Ezekiel to set his face against Gog and prophesy against him.
easy.q: Against whom is Ezekiel commanded to prophesy?

answers: Chief prince of Meshech and Tubal
easy.explanation: Gog is called the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
easy.q: How is Gog identified in these verses?

easy.explanation: The army is described as having bucklers, shields, and swords.
easy.q: What weapons do Gog’s soldiers carry?

medium.explanation: The Lord says, “I will turn thee back, and put hooks into thy jaws.”
medium.q: What does the Lord put into Gog’s jaws?

answers: Gog is preparing to lead a great army
medium.explanation: Many peoples, horses, horsemen, and armed companies gather with Gog.
medium.q: What does the gathering of many peoples with Gog show?

medium.explanation: Gog is told to prepare himself and to be a guard unto his company.
medium.q: What does Gog command his company to be?

answers: It includes horses, horsemen, shields, helmets, and swords
challenge.explanation: The detailed list of troops and weapons presents a large, prepared army.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Gog’s army is organized rather than accidental?

answers: The prophecy identifies Gog and describes the force he will lead
The prophecy concerns only Ezekiel’s personal life
challenge.explanation: The command to prophesy introduces Gog, his identity, and his military preparations.
challenge.q: How are the command to prophesy and the description of the army connected?

answers: Persia, Ethiopia, Libya, Gomer, and Togarmah are named
Only one Israelite tribe is named
challenge.explanation: The named nations and regions show the wide origin of Gog’s forces.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Gog’s army includes peoples from many regions?

paragraphs.title: The Invasion of the Restored Land

easy.explanation: The passage says that Gog will come “in the latter years.”
easy.q: When will Gog come against the land?

answers: A people gathered out of many nations
easy.explanation: The people have been gathered out of many nations and dwell safely.
easy.q: Who lives in the land Gog approaches?

answers: As a land of unwalled villages
easy.explanation: Gog plans to attack a land of unwalled villages whose people have neither bars nor gates.
easy.q: How is the land described by Gog?

answers: Its inhabitants live without walls, bars, or gates
It is filled with foreign armies
medium.explanation: Gog sees the secure but unwalled settlements as an easy target.
medium.q: Why does Gog think the land is suitable for an attack?

answers: To take a spoil and a prey
medium.explanation: Gog says that he will go up to take a spoil and a prey.
medium.q: What is Gog’s purpose in going against the land?

answers: The absence of defensive walls and gates
The mountainous character of the land
medium.explanation: The following words explain that the people dwell without walls, bars, or gates.
medium.q: What does the phrase “unwalled villages” emphasize?

answers: They dwell safely, while Gog plans to exploit them for spoil
They attack Gog, while Gog protects them
They leave the land, while Gog builds homes for them
challenge.explanation: The people live securely, but Gog views their lack of walls as an opportunity for plunder.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the people in the land and Gog’s intention?

answers: Whether he has come to take a spoil and carry away wealth
Whether he will lead Israel’s army
Whether he will build walls around the land
challenge.explanation: They ask whether Gog has gathered his company to take silver, gold, cattle, goods, and spoil.
challenge.q: What do Sheba, Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish ask Gog?

answers: The land dwells safely, Gog sees an easy target, and he plans to plunder it
The land is destroyed, and then its people build an army
The merchants attack, and Gog defends the land
challenge.explanation: The people’s secure condition leads Gog to form an evil plan to seize their possessions.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is presented in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Gog’s Arrival and the Revelation of God’s Holiness

easy.explanation: The Lord says that Gog will come from his place out of the north parts.
easy.q: From what direction will Gog come?

easy.explanation: Gog will come against the Lord’s people of Israel.
The Lord brings Gog so that the heathen may know Him.
easy.q: What will the heathen learn when the Lord brings Gog against the land?

answers: Many people, a great company, and a mighty army
medium.explanation: Gog comes with many people, riders on horses, a great company, and a mighty army.
medium.q: How large is the force that comes with Gog?

answers: So the heathen may know Him when He is sanctified
So Gog may inherit the land
So His power may remain hidden
medium.explanation: The Lord says He will bring Gog so that the nations may know Him when He is sanctified.
medium.q: Why does the Lord bring Gog against His land?

answers: God will reveal His holiness through what happens to Gog
God will give the land to Gog
medium.explanation: Gog’s coming and defeat will reveal God’s holiness before the nations.
medium.q: What does “I will be sanctified in thee” mean in this context?

answers: Israel’s security highlights the unexpected invasion and the Lord’s purpose in it
Israel’s security prevents Gog from arriving
Israel’s security proves that Gog leads Israel
challenge.explanation: Israel dwells safely, yet Gog is brought against the land so the nations will know the Lord.
challenge.q: How are Israel’s security and Gog’s arrival related?

answers: A future period associated with the end of days
A recent event in the past
An event that happens every day
challenge.explanation: The phrase places Gog’s coming in a future, end-time setting.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “in the latter days” indicate?

answers: It presents Gog’s coming as part of things spoken by earlier prophets
It cancels the prophecy concerning Gog
It changes the subject to trade between nations
challenge.explanation: The Lord says that He had spoken of bringing Gog through His servants the prophets of Israel.
challenge.q: How does the reference to former prophets strengthen the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Great Earthquake and the Shaking of the Land

easy.explanation: The passage says, “my fury shall come up in my face.”
easy.q: What rises when Gog comes against the land of Israel?

easy.explanation: The Lord declares that there shall be a great shaking in the land of Israel.
easy.q: What great event will occur in the land?

answers: It will disappear beneath the sea
It will fall to the ground
easy.explanation: The verse says, “every wall shall fall to the ground.”
easy.q: What will happen to every wall?

answers: Fish, birds, animals, creeping things, and people
medium.explanation: The passage lists creatures of the sea, heaven, field, earth, and all people.
medium.q: Who or what will be affected by the shaking?

answers: The mountains, steep places, and walls
medium.explanation: The mountains will be thrown down, the steep places will fall, and every wall will collapse.
medium.q: Which parts of the landscape will fall?

answers: Sloping or terraced parts of the land
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to elevated or sloping features of the land that will fall during the shaking.
medium.q: What are “steep places” in the context of the passage?

answers: The shaking will have a widespread effect across the land
Only the army will be harmed
The animals will lead the army
challenge.explanation: The list shows that the shaking affects living creatures throughout the land, not merely the soldiers.
challenge.q: What does the mention of animals and people together emphasize?

answers: The shaking is presented as part of the Lord’s judgment when Gog comes
The shaking has no connection with Gog
challenge.explanation: The great shaking occurs in the context of the Lord’s fury against Gog.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the Lord’s fury and the shaking?

answers: The sea, heaven, field, earth, mountains, and walls are all mentioned
challenge.explanation: The many locations and creatures named show the broad extent of the disturbance.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the destruction is not limited to one place?

paragraphs.title: The Defeat of Gog’s Armies and the Sanctification of God’s Name

answers: The soldiers will fight one another
They will all flee into the sea
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “every man’s sword shall be against his brother.”
easy.q: What will happen within Gog’s armies?

answers: Pestilence, blood, rain, hailstones, fire, and brimstone
easy.explanation: The passage lists pestilence, blood, overflowing rain, great hailstones, fire, and brimstone.
easy.q: By what means will Gog and his armies be judged?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “they shall know that I am the Lord.”
easy.q: What will the nations know after these events?

answers: Through internal fighting and heavenly judgments
medium.explanation: The armies will fight one another and also suffer the Lord’s plagues and storms.
medium.q: How will Gog’s armies be defeated?

answers: The defeat will cause the nations to know the Lord and His holiness
The defeat will hide God’s power
The defeat will make the nations forget the Lord
medium.explanation: The Lord will magnify and sanctify Himself, and many nations will know Him.
medium.q: What is the connection between Gog’s defeat and the sanctification of God’s name?

answers: They are part of the heavenly judgment against Gog’s armies
medium.explanation: The hailstones are listed with rain, fire, and brimstone as instruments of judgment.
medium.q: What are the “great hailstones” used for in the passage?

challenge.explanation: The Lord says that He will call for a sword, plead against Gog, and rain judgments upon him.
challenge.q: Who is described as bringing about the main judgments against Gog?

answers: The great army collapses from within
The passage is describing trade between nations
challenge.explanation: The sword among the armies turns their own strength into a cause of defeat.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the soldiers fight one another?

answers: Gog comes, the Lord judges him, and the nations recognize the Lord
The merchants arrive and build walls
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with the Lord magnifying and sanctifying Himself before many nations.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the purpose of the events in this chapter?
